messages:
Mira S.: heads up — our secret-scanner just flagged a public gist that contains what looks like the deploy SSH key for `redwood-staging-deploy`. discovered by OSS crawler: https://gist.github.com/xxxx :eyes:

devsec-bot: ALERT: high-confidence secret exposure detected (scanner:v2) — token_kind=deploy_key repo_hint=infra-deploy discovered_ts=1869998870

Alex R.: thanks Mira. severity? can someone confirm whether that exact key material is also authorized in prod? :thinking_face:

Sam T.: pinging infra owners. Mira — can you paste the key fingerprint or the private key header so we can grep?

Mira S.: fingerprint: SHA256:AbCdEf1234567890
I grepped across org and found entries referencing that fingerprint in:
- repos/redwood/infra-deploy (deploy keys)
- repos/redwood/staging-worker (authorized_keys)
- terraform/modules/deploy/key.tf (kms-wrapped blob)

Snippet:
```
repos/redwood/infra-deploy/keys.json: {"id":12345, "title":"staging-deploy-key", "fingerprint":"SHA256:AbCdEf1234567890"}
```

Jen K.: OK plan proposal (short):
1) immediately revoke the exposed key from any GitHub repo that lists it
2) rotate any matching key material in Vault/KMS (create new keypair, rewrap secrets)
3) push updated deploy keys into infra (CI secrets, k8s, terraform state) using ephemeral creds where possible
4) enable extra audit logging for the affected key operations and capture full repro timeline
5) post-rotation scans and a quick canary deploy to staging, then prod

Alex R.: +1. Timeline: immediate revoke (within 15m), rotate and rewrap (2h), CI/infra rollout (4–12h), verification & ramp (24h). We should also open an incident ticket and set channel to incident for pager visibility.

Leo (oncall): I can take the revoke step now. Will coordinate with GitHub owners.

Sam T.: listing specific commands for the revoke/rotate ops so nobody improvises differently:
- Revoke via GitHub API (replace ids):
```
# delete deploy key
gh api -X DELETE /repos/redwood/infra-deploy/keys/12345
# verify remaining keys
gh api /repos/redwood/infra-deploy/keys
```
- Rotate keypair (on infra bastion)
```
ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -f /tmp/new-deploy -N ''
# upload public to repo as new deploy key
gh ssh-key add /tmp/new-deploy.pub --title "rotated-staging-1869998888"
```
- Vault/KMS rewrap (example GCP KMS + Vault wrapped blob):
```
# rewrap with new KMS key
gcloud kms keys versions create --key=redwood-deploy-key --keyring=infra-kr --location=global
# then re-encrypt secret in Vault (example)
vault write transit/rewrap ciphertext=@wrapped_blob --key=new-kms-key
```

Mira S.: note: terraform references a kms-wrapped blob in `modules/deploy/key.tf`. we'll need a terraform plan/apply to update state after rewrap. tagging @jen for Terraform runbook.

Jen K.: I'll take TF. steps:
- create new secret in secret manager/vault
- update terraform var to point to new secret id
- run `terraform plan` and `terraform apply -auto-approve` in infra pipeline with approvals

Alex R.: RBAC followups: remove write privileges from service accounts that previously could upload deploy keys; convert long-lived service accounts to workload identity/short-lived tokens where possible. Add to checklist: list of 3 SAs to lock down.

Sam T.: I ran quick queries; SAs with write access: infra-ci-sa, legacy-deploy-sa, staging-helper-sa. Recommend revoking and replacing with ephemeral tokens for infra-ci-sa first.

Leo (oncall): I've deleted the deploy key from infra-deploy (gh api returned 204). leaving a note in the repo audit. Will also tag the PR that added it originally. :white_check_mark:

Mira S.: good. next: rotate the KMS-wrapped secret and push new private key into Vault so CI can use it. I can generate keypair and share encrypted blob via ops channel when ready.

devsec-bot: NOTE: Audit logging for GitHub org already shows key creation event at 2025-09-02T14:22:11Z by user: legacy-ops-bot. Retention window set to 90d; copied snapshot to secure bucket: gs://redwood-security-archive/1869998888-snapshot.json

Jen K.: After TF apply, I'll kick a canary deploy to staging and run a smoke test:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_TOKEN" https://staging-api.redwood.ai/health || echo "canary failed"
```
If canary passes, we schedule prod push in the evening (low traffic).

Alex R.: ACTIONS (assign):
- Leo: revoke in GH (done) and post audit link (in progress)
- Mira: generate new keypair + wrap in KMS + write to Vault (in 2h)
- Jen: update TF and run infra apply, canary deploy (in 4h)
- Sam: RBAC cleanup ticket and rotate SAs to ephemeral (in 24h)
- Alex: own incident comms and postmortem

Sam T.: also recommend blocking the original gist URL at org level and filing takedown with gist provider. I've filed takedown ticket #TT-8812.

Mira S.: uploading new key blob to Vault now (encrypted). vault path: secret/data/infra/deploy/staging-rotated-1869998888 (will share ACLs once created).

Leo (oncall): posting audit links here: https://github.com/orgs/redwood/settings/audit-logs?since=2025-09-02&actor=legacy-ops-bot — saved to incident ticket.

Alex R.: nice work. once Jen confirms canary success we can close the immediate incident. we'll schedule a follow-up RFC to move deploy keys to ephemeral signing via SSH CA and remove long-lived deploy keys entirely.

Mira S.: can everyone react with :thumbsup: when you've finished your assigned task so we can track? I'll keep the thread updated.

(12 minutes later)
Jen K.: canary pass in staging. smoke tests green. preparing prod rollout window at 02:00 UTC.

Sam T.: RBAC ticket created: SEC-1342 — list of SAs and proposed least-priv changes attached.

Alex R.: closing immediate incident after prod rollout. Postmortem owners: Alex, Mira, Jen. Populating timeline and remediation items into SEC-INC-20250902.

Mira S.: thanks team. we'll add automated gist scanning rule to CI and block commits that include private key headers. Also updating docs for incident runbook. :lock:
